name: vix_bucket_strategy_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: India VIX provides a forward-looking measure of expected market volatility derived from NIFTY option prices. By bucketing VIX into 4 regimes — Calm (VIX < 13), Normal (13-18), Elevated (18-24), and Crisis (> 24) — and assigning a different strategy to each bucket, we adapt to the macroeconomic uncertainty environment. Calm: aggressive mean-reversion (small moves revert quickly). Normal: standard EMA crossover momentum. Elevated: reduced size, wide-stop trend following. Crisis: flat (no edge, too noisy). The inefficiency persists because most retail traders use the same strategy regardless of VIX level, and VIX-conditional strategy selection requires monitoring an external data feed.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; varies by VIX bucket
hold_time: CALM: 10-20 min; NORMAL: 20-45 min; ELEVATED: 30-90 min

indicators.name: VIX_Bucket
indicators.params: CALM if VIX < 13; NORMAL if 13 <= VIX < 18; ELEVATED if 18 <= VIX < 24; CRISIS if VIX >= 24

conditions: CALM: close < BB_lower_calm AND close < vwap AND RSI(close,10) < 30
NORMAL: EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
ELEVATED: close > Supertrend(10,4.0) AND close > vwap AND volume > 2*SMA(volume,20)
long.confirmation: CALM: uptick (close > close[-1]); NORMAL: volume > SMA(volume,15); ELEVATED: Supertrend hold for 3 bars

conditions: CALM: close > BB_upper_calm AND close > vwap AND RSI(close,10) > 70
NORMAL: EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
ELEVATED: close < Supertrend(10,4.0) AND close < vwap AND volume > 2*SMA(volume,20)
short.confirmation: CALM: downtick (close < close[-1]); NORMAL: volume > SMA(volume,15); ELEVATED: Supertrend hold for 3 bars

exit.target: CALM: 20 bps; NORMAL: 35 bps; ELEVATED: 60 bps
exit.stop_loss: CALM: 12 bps; NORMAL: 20 bps; ELEVATED: 35 bps
exit.trailing_stop: CALM: none (quick target); NORMAL: 12 bps after 20 bps; ELEVATED: 25 bps after 35 bps
exit.time_stop: CALM: 20 bars; NORMAL: 45 bars; ELEVATED: 90 bars
exit.signal_exit: VIX_Bucket transitions to a different bucket — exit and re-evaluate

risk.position_sizing: CALM: ₹1.5L (large, small moves); NORMAL: ₹1L; ELEVATED: ₹50K (small, large moves); CRISIS: ₹0 (flat)

filters.vix_filter: VIX_Bucket itself is the primary filter — CRISIS bucket = no trading
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 or after 15:10; CALM can trade until 15:15
filters.volume_filter: ELEVATED: strict 2x volume required; CALM/NORMAL: SMA(volume,15) sufficient
filters.trend_filter: NORMAL: NIFTY trend must agree; CALM/ELEVATED: no trend filter
filters.spread_filter: CALM: spread < 3 bps; NORMAL: < 5 bps; ELEVATED: < 8 bps
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day in all buckets; skip all entries on RBI policy day
other_filters: VIX must have been in current bucket for at least 15 min before entry

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — VIX bucket strategy selection is intuitive but requires discipline to switch strategies dynamically; most traders stick with one approach regardless of VIX

weaknesses: VIX bucket boundaries (13, 18, 24) are arbitrary and may not represent true regime shifts — the optimal boundaries likely vary over multi-year cycles as structural volatility changes
India VIX can jump from 14 to 19 within minutes during a shock, causing an immediate regime switch and forced exit from current position at a loss
CRISIS bucket (VIX > 24) has historically offered some of the best mean-reversion opportunities, but the strategy avoids them entirely, missing high-conviction trades
prior_art: VIX-conditional strategies common in US equity options trading; Whaley (2009) on VIX; VIX-based strategy selection discussed in Sinclair's 'Volatility Trading'; India VIX-specific research limited
notes: Consider adding a 5th bucket for 'extremely calm' (VIX < 10) which historically precedes vol spikes — could be used as a warning signal to reduce overall exposure. The CRISIS bucket could allow very selective high-conviction trades with tight stops.
